instruction: I've been reading several interesting blog posts today. Please save the currently open blog articles as PDF files to my Downloads folder at /home/user/Downloads.

metadata.explanation: Task requires downloading 2 blog articles as PDFs to the Downloads directory. Evaluator verifies exactly 2 PDF files exist in /home/user/Downloads. Custom getter lists PDF files in directory, metric checks count matches expected value of 2.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly extracts PDF file list from target directory using bash command
Metric correctly compares PDF count against expected value of 2
Data flow is correct: getter returns list of filenames, metric counts and compares
Expected value (2) correctly matches the number of blog URLs opened in config
Parameter handling is correct: metric properly accesses 'count' from rules dict when expected.type='rule'
LIMITATION: Evaluator only verifies count, not content or origin of PDFs - cannot distinguish between pre-existing PDFs and newly saved blog articles
LIMITATION: No verification that PDFs actually contain the blog article content or originate from the specified URLs
In isolated test environments where Downloads folder starts empty, count-based verification is acceptable but not ideal
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding timestamp-based filtering to only count PDFs created after task start time
Consider adding filename pattern matching to verify PDFs have expected names (e.g., contain keywords from blog titles)
Consider adding file size validation to ensure PDFs are non-empty and reasonable size for blog articles
For more robust verification, could check PDF metadata (creation time, page count) or extract text to verify content matches blog URLs
